## What you build today

A flashed G431 ESC talking to your laptop over serial, with the angular sensor
wired on SPI3 and the motor spinning under commander control.

![How the battery, ESC, encoder, motor and microcontroller connect. The XIAO nRF52840 shown here is the separate-microcontroller option for serial described below --- note that TX and RX are crossed. SPI3 and UART pin assignments match the rework in @tbl-spi3 and *ST-Link serial*.](/Fig/xiao-esc-wiring-diagram.png){#fig-wiring width=6.5in}

Work through the module with this diagram open: every step below either wires
one of these links or configures it in firmware.

## Firmware

Code for the B-G431B-ESC1 motor controller, using the SimpleFOC library, is in
the lab repository: [FAAV-G431-ESC](https://github.com/MIT-AURA-Lab/FAAV-G431-ESC).
See [Software](/reference/software.qmd) for all repositories.

## Commanding and monitoring

This is a high-level summary of [the SimpleFOC communication docs](https://docs.simplefoc.com/communication).
Communication with the ESC is over **serial**, either via the ST-Link
programmer (the small attached board) or via a separate microcontroller board.

Once serial is established at **115200 baud**, you interact with the ESC
through the **commander** --- a practical interface for setting and getting
values ([instructions](https://docs.simplefoc.com/commander_motor)). Ask the
commander for available commands with `?`. Currently available:

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `M` | Full motor configuration |
| `F` | Get the main loop frequency |
| `L` | Turn the onboard LED on and off (useful as a comms check) |
| `T` | Set the target value --- rad, rad/s or N/m depending on control mode |
| `W` | Watchdog on/off. If no new target arrives for 1 s, target is set to zero. **On by default** |
| `R` | `R0`/`R1` disable/enable a linear ramp when changing setpoint. `RD1000` sets ramp duration to 1000 ms (default 1000 ms). Off by default |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Careful when changing control mode

`T` means something different in each mode --- position, velocity, or torque.
Sending a velocity setpoint while in torque mode will do something you did not
intend, with the wings attached.
:::

## ST-Link serial

The ST-Link needs to be connected to the ESC MCU. Out of the box that happens
via **Serial2**, but not once those GPIOs are used as SPI3 for the sensor. In
that case you must connect **Serial1** to the ST-Link:

1. Disconnect USART2 and connect USART1: remove **R23** and **R24** on the
   daughter board (desolder).
2. Solder wires to the now-free pins of R23/R24 --- the pads closer to U3,
   further away from the USB port. Connect the wire from **R23** to the pad for
   hall sensor 2 (**PB7**), and the wire from **R24** to the pad for hall
   sensor 1 (**PB6**) on J8.
3. Remap the pins in software for SPI use: in `platformio.ini` via
   `build_flags`, and by overwriting the `WEAK PinMap`s in `pinmap_custom.h`.
   See commit `18520ac` on GitHub for details.

## Angular sensor on SPI3

There is no SPI link exposed directly on the board. The solution is to use the
**SPI3 bus**, exposed through a few hardware modifications and matching
software changes. @fig-wiring shows the four signals in context, including the
MOSI tap on R14 that shares the BEMF divider.

| | SCLK | MISO | MOSI | CS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **MCU GPIO** | PB3 | PB4 | PB5 | PA15 |
| **G431B pin** | J3 | J3 | R14\* | J3 |

: SPI3 connections on the G431. \* Solder onto the outward side of the resistor. {#tbl-spi3}

![GPIOs of the G431B-ESC1 board](/Fig/b431g.jpg){#fig-g431-gpio}

::: {.callout-note}
## Checkpoint --- TA sign-off

Commander responds to `?` over serial at 115200 baud, `L` toggles the onboard
LED, the sensor returns a plausible angle through a full manual rotation, and
the motor spins under a `T` command.
:::
